evidence:
FR-CP-003 (scope isolation) is genuinely met. I verified the implementation AND the test against both source and the built dist that the test runs.

AC: "current-slice refs are NOT listed as done merely from a worker claim."
- x:/repositories/agent-swarm/src/cli.ts:4440-4462 buildLedgerSettledFacts iterates coverage.ledger.entries and at line 4442 explicitly skips entry.sliceId === slice.id, so the current slice's own refs can NEVER become a settled fact regardless of evidence. (dist mirror: dist/cli.js:3967.)
- Deeper proof that a worker claim cannot manufacture a "done"/settled ledger status at all: src/observability.ts:293-299 latestFrAcResults reads ONLY evidence of kind "command" with a frAcResults array — kind "worker_result" is ignored entirely. The ref coverage status becomes "done" only via frAcResult.status passed/human_verified or (lease completed AND owning slice accepted) (src/observability.ts:660-672), and verification is set from frAcResult.status (line 732). directLedgerStatus (src/observability.ts:905-926) then derives accepted/verified/review_passed/human_verified strictly from that durable verification/review/sliceStatus state. So a worker_result claim with payload {status:"passed"} produces no frAcResult and no settled status. (dist mirror: dist/observability.js:242.)

AC: "accepted sibling refs used as context ONLY when the ledger shows accepted/passed evidence."
- SETTLED_LEDGER_STATUSES = accepted/verified/human_verified/review_passed (src/cli.ts:96); only entries with these statuses become acceptedSiblings (src/cli.ts:4443-4454), each carrying its durable evidenceIds.

AC: "blocked/human refs stay visibly blocked."
- BLOCKED_LEDGER_STATUSES (src/cli.ts:97) routes blocked/human_input_required/failed/awaiting_human_verification into a separate blockedRefs list (src/cli.ts:4455-4461), rendered under "Still-blocked / human-gated refs (NOT settled...)" (src/cli.ts:4484-4492).

AC: "tests cover >=1 accepted sibling ref AND >=1 current in-scope ref to prove the distinction."
- tests/settled-facts.e2e.test.js:276-323 sets up an ACCEPTED sibling slice (AC-INV-001.1, status accepted, with a command-evidence frAcResults entry status=passed, evidence EVID-settled-sibling) AND a current in-scope slice (AC-INV-002.1, status ready) that has ONLY a worker_result claim with payload {status:"passed"} (test lines 187-225), PLUS a blocked ref (AC-INV-003.1, lines 227-268). It dispatches the in-scope slice with --driver fixture, reads the persisted worker prompt, and asserts: the sibling appears as "AC-INV-001.1 (accepted)" with "EVID-settled-sibling" (lines 295-296); the in-scope ref is NOT listed as accepted/verified in the accepted region (lines 301-308) and instead appears only in the "produce fresh per-FR/AC evidence for every in-scope ref (AC-INV-002.1)" obligation sentence (lines 309-313); the blocked ref renders "AC-INV-003.1 (blocked)" and is never (accepted) (lines 316-322). This exercises both the accepted-sibling AND in-scope-ref distinction exactly as the AC demands.

I executed the test against the built dist: `node --test tests/settled-facts.e2e.test.js` -> 1 pass, 0 fail. dist is newer than src and contains the worker_result-ignoring filter, the entry.sliceId===slice.id skip, and the SETTLED set (verified via grep on dist/cli.js / dist/observability.js).

Additive: buildWorkerPrompt input.settledFacts is OPTIONAL (src/cli.ts:6645 settledFacts?:) and formatSettledFactsForPrompt tolerates undefined (src/cli.ts:4466, facts?.acceptedSiblings ?? []), so existing prompt consumers that omit it keep working. The field is appended into the existing prompt template (src/cli.ts:6692) without removing/altering prior sections.

Model-agnostic: settled-facts derivation operates purely on the SwarmStore/coverage ledger (src/cli.ts:4406-4464) with zero provider branching. It is invoked on the single shared executeWorkerRun dispatch path (src/cli.ts:2368, 2407) where driverId is resolved generically for fixture/codex/claude (src/cli.ts:2384-2387) and the prompt is built BEFORE any driver-specific execution. The revive path uses the same buildLedgerSettledFacts (src/cli.ts:1656). No Claude-only code path.
gaps: No acceptance gaps for FR-CP-003. Minor, non-blocking observations (do not affect acceptance): (1) The negative test assertion at tests/settled-facts.e2e.test.js:305-308 relies on a verification-set status suffix regex within the region before the "Still-blocked" marker; this is defensible but is a string-shape assertion rather than a structural ledger assertion — if the prompt wording later changed it could give false confidence. The underlying isolation is nonetheless enforced structurally in code (slice-id skip + worker_result ignored by latestFrAcResults), so the protection does not depend solely on prompt wording. (2) The scope-isolation guarantee depends on latestFrAcResults restricting to kind==="command" evidence; this is correct today but is an implicit invariant — if a future change let worker_result evidence feed frAcResults, the slice-id skip at cli.ts:4442 would still protect the current slice's own refs, but a worker could then influence a SIBLING ref's status. Out of scope for this slice; flagged only as a latent coupling.

gaps: Minor, non-blocking: the test that hits the ACTUAL HTTP route (tests/web-server.e2e.test.js:457-465) asserts only the intervention field's shape/enum membership, not a concrete classification value. The tests asserting a specific deterministic classification for a named failure class (valid_artifact_hung_child, missing_result) consume the CLI `inspect ... --json` path rather than the HTTP route.
